method: I approached the lecture by analysing how artists transform information and research into creative experiences. I focused on the relationship between data, visualisation and storytelling, particularly how digital tools can communicate complex environmental and social issues to an audience.
related_work: Several projects discussed in class influenced my thinking. Extinction Gong uses real-time extinction data to create an artistic response to biodiversity loss. Liam Young and Unknown Fields' Rare Earthenware explores the environmental consequences of rare earth mining. Bobby Pietrusko's In Plain Sight examines how satellite images shape our understanding of the Earth and globalisation.
conclusion_future_work: For my future work, I would like to explore how digital technology and visual storytelling can communicate social or environmental issues. I am interested in experimenting with data visualisation and interactive media, while developing a project that encourages audiences to question their relationship with technology and the wider world.
results_discussion:
The lecture changed the way I think about the role of art and design. I was particularly surprised by the idea of speculative design, which does not necessarily aim to provide solutions but instead encourages people to question existing systems and imagine alternative futures.

Rare Earthenware was especially interesting to me because it reveals the environmental costs hidden behind everyday technologies such as smartphones and electric vehicles. It made me realise that technological progress can also create serious environmental problems. Extinction Gong also demonstrated how data can become an emotional and powerful artistic experience rather than simply numerical information.

Bobby Pietrusko's projects further showed me how satellite technology and visual data can influence our understanding of the world. In Plain Sight was particularly interesting because the Blue Marble and Black Marble images present different perspectives of the same planet.

Overall, I learned that art and technology can be used not only to create visual experiences but also to challenge social assumptions and encourage critical thinking. I would like to explore how data, visual storytelling and interactive media could become part of my own creative practice.
title: week 8
introduction: This week, I explored the relationship between art, design and technology through the history of Bauhaus and the concept of speculative design. I was particularly interested in how contemporary artists use data, technology and creative experiments to question global issues and encourage people to think differently about the future.
